complexity.notes: Correct but far from optimal — the BST property allows a simple O(h) walk comparing values. The copied isSameTree/isSubtree methods are dead weight for this problem and make the code harder to read; note isSubtree is only O(n) per call here because unique values make isSameTree fail in O(1) except at the single matching node.
complexity.summary: Ignores the BST ordering and instead reuses isSameTree/isSubtree helpers: at each node it checks whether p contains q (or vice versa), whether p and q split across the children, and otherwise recurses. Each node visit costs O(n) in subtree scans and up to O(n) nodes are visited, giving O(n^2) worst case on a degenerate tree.
